chapter_title: Chương 129: Ghi hình chương trình thì cứ việc đấu võ mồm.

segments.title: Chương 129: Ghi hình chương trình thì cứ việc đấu võ mồm.
segments.content:
Chapter 132: Recording a Show Is All About Trash Talk

The first TV show Chen Guiliang participated in was quite a big deal: CCTV's "Dialogue."

This show had a long run; it was still on the air before Chen Guiliang was reborn.

Invited guests included foreign dignitaries like Hillary Clinton, business magnates like the Mas big and small, Buffett, and Bill Gates, as well as cultural and sports celebrities like Jin Yong, Liu Cixin, Old Man Yimou, Andy Lau, and Yao Ming.

The number of these big shots was limited, so they couldn't be invited every week. Most of the time, the guests were not as high-profile.

For example, four years ago, Han Han was invited to record an episode of "Dialogue" and was besieged by other guests and the live audience. The host was from Hunan TV, and the latter half of the show was a disaster, with the situation spiraling out of the host's control.

"Hello, Chen Guiliang." The host, Miss Shen, came to the studio's backstage area.

Chen Guiliang smiled and shook her hand. "Hello, Miss Shen."

Chen Guiliang had long heard of this Miss Shen, mainly remembering two news stories about her later on.

One was a sports story: Miss Shen served as an Olympic torchbearer.

The other was a crime story: Miss Shen did some time in prison a certain year.

But it was undeniable that Miss Shen's hosting skills were far superior to the Ms. Wang from Han Han's episode.

"Today's main topic is whether university students can balance entrepreneurship and their studies," Miss Shen said, giving Chen Guiliang a heads-up. "We've invited two doctoral advisors and a senior executive from a publicly listed company as special guests. They might ask some sharp questions, and the live audience might also give you a hard time."

Chen Guiliang nodded. "Understood."

As they were talking, another person came in. It was Wang Xiaochuan, the project lead for Sogou.

At 15, he won first prize in the National Mathematics Olympiad and was granted early admission to high school. At 16, he used his personal computer to complete all the proofs for elementary geometry propositions. At 18, he won a gold medal in a subject competition and was granted early admission to Tsinghua University's Department of Computer Science. At 25, he earned his master's degree from Tsinghua.

"Hello."

"Hello."

The two shook hands and sat down, waiting for the show to start recording.

Wang Xiaochuan said, "I'm from Rongcheng."

"A fellow townsman," Chen Guiliang said with a smile. "My girlfriend is also from Rongcheng."

Wang Xiaochuan said, "Your Xiaonei Net is doing very well. I used to be a part-time employee at Xiaoyoulu; I developed many of its features."

"Then you're a senior in the field," Chen Guiliang said.

Facing the boss of Xiaonei Net, Wang Xiaochuan felt extremely conflicted.

Xiaoyoulu was a project he worked on part-time during his undergraduate years. Sohu disbanded Xiaoyoulu's founding team but had him lead the Sogou search engine project instead. They even entrusted him with great responsibility, promoting him step-by-step from senior technical manager to senior technical director.

The next step was a promotion to Vice President of Sohu!

He had also suggested to his boss multiple times that they should innovate Xiaoyoulu, but Mr. Zhang had always brushed him off.

Before long, two more people arrived.

One was an old acquaintance, Professor Shang from the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, the one who wrote the preface for "Those Things in the Ming Dynasty."

The other was Professor Yang from the Chinese Language and Literature Department at Beijing Normal University.

Everyone was very cordial.

Professor Yang even said to Chen Guiliang, "I might be a bit sharp with my words. Don't mind it when the time comes."

Chen Guiliang said, "Professor Yang, please say whatever you'd like. I'll humbly accept any criticism."

The Han Han episode had caused quite a stir. The show certainly achieved its desired effect, but the host was sent back from CCTV to a local station. Her hosting skills were just too poor!

The show officially began recording.

The host and the three special guests went to the studio first for an opening discussion, while Chen Guiliang continued to wait backstage.

Dozens of live audience members were already seated.

The host, Miss Shen, began: "There's a student who has sparked public discussion multiple times this year. He once earned a special admission spot at Peking University through the New Concept Composition Contest, which then embroiled him in a vortex of public opinion about fairness in admissions. Then, during the Gaokao, he scored high enough to surpass Peking University's admission cutoff. In front of dozens of media reporters, he also set a small goal for himself to earn one hundred million during his university years. He also publicly questioned errors in high school Chinese language textbooks..."

"Recently, he founded Xiaonei Net and launched a campus belle and beau contest, and published the full-length historical work 'Those Things in the Ming Dynasty'..."

"Today, we have invited..."

"Professor Shang, what is your impression of Chen Guiliang?"

Professor Shang smiled. "A very good student. I hope he considers majoring in history. I wrote the preface for 'Those Things in the Ming Dynasty' partly to help popularize knowledge of Ming Dynasty history among the public."

"And you, Professor Yang?" Miss Shen asked.

Professor Yang said, "I particularly admire his poem, 'Voyage on the Boundless Sea.' I think he could pursue a major in Chinese literature."

After a bit more chat, Miss Shen introduced the topic: "Many university students start businesses, but they often drop out midway. Moreover, Chen Guiliang started his business right at the beginning of his freshman year. Is he too eager to do business? Can entrepreneurship and academics be balanced?"

Wang Xiaochuan shook his head. "It's very difficult to balance. I started working part-time at Chinaren in my junior year, and I continued part-time when I moved to Sohu. Let alone starting a business, even a full-time job would have affected my studies. From my junior year to my graduate school graduation, I worked part-time for a total of four years. I only started working full-time after getting my master's degree."

Professor Yang said, "Starting a business as a freshman is too early; you haven't even finished your foundational courses. I believe that even if you want to start a business, you should wait until your junior year."

"It's very hard to manage both," Professor Shang said with a smile. "Why don't we make a bet? Chen Guiliang will last until his junior year at most before dropping out. He's in the Yuanpei Program, where the academic workload is extremely heavy. He'll probably fail several courses this semester."

After some more back and forth, Miss Shen stood up and said, "Let's welcome our guest for tonight..."

Chen Guiliang walked out, smiling and waving, as the audience applauded.

He shook hands with the host and the three guests, then returned to his seat.

"Did you hear all of that just now? Is there anything you'd like to say in your defense?" Miss Shen asked.

Chen Guiliang said, "The three seniors are all correct. I don't recommend that freshmen start businesses. It will definitely affect your studies. If the business fails, then both your career and your academics are ruined."

"But you still chose to start a business," Miss Shen said.

Chen Guiliang said, "I'm different."

Miss Shen asked, "Why are you different?"

Chen Guiliang said, "Because I believe I can succeed."

The host, guests, and audience all laughed. Some were laughing mockingly, thinking Chen Guiliang was too arrogant.

These were real audience members, not plants hired by the show.

And there was no shortage of people with bizarre opinions.

During the Han Han episode, there was even a conversation like this—

Female audience member: "What chat software do you use online? OICQ or ICQ?"

Han Han: "I use chat rooms."

Female audience member: "If you want to grow up, you should use OICQ and ICQ. That's the world of adults."

Han Han: "Haha, thanks."

Miss Shen asked, "Professor Yang, are there many students at your university who start businesses?"

Professor Yang said, "Quite a few, but most of them fail. Not just at our university, but all over China and the world, most student entrepreneurs will fail. The successful ones are few and far between. We can't say that just because Bill Gates succeeded, we will too. I believe university students should be very cautious about entrepreneurship. Especially freshmen and sophomores. If you haven't learned your foundational courses well and then your business fails, your entire future is ruined."

Miss Shen then asked Chen Guiliang, "Why do you think you will definitely succeed?"

"Because my project is good," Chen Guiliang said. "In the field of campus online social networking, there's not a single competitor in the country that can put up a fight."

Wang Xiaochuan said, "It's very difficult to monetize a campus-based online community."

Chen Guiliang smiled. "Are you saying Sohu's Xiaoyoulu is on its last legs? The reason you at Sohu aren't doing well is because there's a problem with the brains and vision of Sohu's upper management."

The moment he said this, the entire audience was in an uproar.

At this time, Sohu was still one of the three major web portals. Everyone thought Sohu was amazing; it hadn't yet become an object of ridicule.

Chen Guiliang's statement was like saying the Mas, big and small, had no business sense during their peak!

Chen Guiliang continued, "Sohu abandoning Xiaoyoulu was a grave strategic error. I can understand Sohu doing MMS, since it's a way to make a lot of quick cash. But their other businesses are spread too thin. A hit here, a tap there. It looks like a comprehensive layout, but it actually lacks focus. We're in the Web 2.0 era now, but the thinking of Sohu's management is still stuck two or three years in the past."

Wang Xiaochuan said, "We do have a focus: Sogou Search and Sohu Mall."

Chen Guiliang said, "If I were Mr. Zhang, I'd definitely fire the person in charge of Sohu Mall. It's a total mess!"

Miss Shen thought to herself: This guy is so arrogant, but the ratings are secure.

Miss Shen smiled and guided the conversation, "How about you comment on Sina, Netease, and Baidu as well?"

Chen Guiliang began to unleash his big moves. "With the arrival of the Web 2.0 era, the portal websites are destined to decline."

"Netease transitioned early, and will probably focus on gaming in the future. But the Netease News comment section is a cesspool. I feel dirty just looking at it."

"Sina News is about the same. If Sina doesn't find a core business soon, it's not far from death's door."

"Baidu's search business can hold on for a few more years, but it will decline within a decade. Tieba is a pretty good product, though. But with Baidu's current model, Tieba will sooner or later be run into the ground by Baidu itself."

"None of them are any good. They're already outdated. The future of the internet belongs to the young people!"

Wang Xiaochuan didn't know whether to laugh or cry. He knew Chen Guiliang was trying to generate hype.

Professor Yang said, "Young people shouldn't be too arrogant. They should humbly learn and improve themselves."

"If you're not arrogant, are you even still young?" Chen Guiliang retorted.

Miss Shen asked, "Have you made any money yet?"

"No," Chen Guiliang said. "I've poured all my manuscript fees and prize money into it, and I've also taken out a 500,000 RMB loan from the Peking University Science Park. I'll also continue to invest the royalties from 'Those Things in the Ming Dynasty' into Xiaonei Net. In half a year at most, I'll be able to secure my first round of investment."

"What if no firms invest?" Wang Xiaochuan asked.

Chen Guiliang said, "Then it means the venture capitalists have no vision, like seeing gold on the roadside and not knowing to pick it up."

"Can I say something?"

A middle-aged woman in the audience couldn't hold it in any longer.

Miss Shen signaled for a staff member to pass her the microphone.

The middle-aged woman said, "I bought a set of your 'Those Things in the Ming Dynasty' for my child. It's indeed very well-written. I hear you can also write classical poetry; you're a very outstanding young man. You worked so hard to get into Peking University, why can't you just focus on your studies, and write articles in your spare time to earn fame and royalties? Have you considered your parents? They worked so hard to put you through school. What if your company fails?"

"But I won't fail," Chen Guiliang said with a smile.

The middle-aged woman said, "You yourself just said you're carrying a 500,000 RMB loan. That's a huge amount of money!"

Chen Guiliang didn't explain further to the woman. Instead, he asked Wang Xiaochuan, "How about we make a bet?"

"What kind of bet?" Wang Xiaochuan asked.

Chen Guiliang said, "Within one year, Xiaonei Net's valuation will reach 10 million US dollars."

Wang Xiaochuan shook his head. "I won't bet."

Miss Shen asked, "Why not?"

Wang Xiaochuan smiled but said nothing.

Chen Guiliang said, "Let me explain. He doesn't want to bet because there's a chance he might lose."

"Ooh!"

The young people in the audience started to hoot.

That middle-aged woman picked up the microphone again. "Students should study hard and not waste their precious time. We didn't have the opportunity back then. You were born in a good era; you shouldn't just be thinking about making money."

Miss Shen asked, "Do you think that statement is correct?"

"This lady is right, but I'd like to add something," Chen Guiliang said. "Learning is a lifelong process. It doesn't just happen on campus, nor is it confined to textbooks. When talking about education, Einstein said something I find very true: 'Education is what remains after one has forgotten everything he learned in school.'"

The woman expressed her doubt. "Did Einstein say that? What education is there to talk about if you've forgotten all the knowledge?"

Chen Guiliang said, "Because the essence of education is not limited to imparting knowledge, but more importantly, it's about cultivating a person's way of thinking, character, and values. Compared to knowledge itself, these latter three are more important."

Miss Shen said, "The topic has shifted back to education. What are the two professors' thoughts?"

Professor Shang said, "I agree with this view. Knowledge can be acquired at any time, but once one's way of thinking, character, and values are formed, they are very difficult to change."

"This is indeed the core of education," Professor Yang said. "Most of the knowledge from high school and university will be slowly forgotten after one enters the workforce. But the fundamental qualities cultivated in students through the teaching of this knowledge will accompany them for the rest of their lives."

Miss Shen smiled. "There's a young audience member over there who's been raising his hand for a while. Let's pass him the microphone."

A high school student stood up. "Chen Guiliang, what you were just talking about, is that quality education?"

"What is quality education?" Chen Guiliang asked in return.

The high school student said, "It's about respecting students' natural talents and strengths, and not judging them solely based on scores. It should be like in the United States, where students freely choose subjects they like, and other assessments for interests and special skills are added. There shouldn't be so much homework, leaving students with more free time. This is the way to improve a student's comprehensive abilities."

Chen Guiliang asked, "So the Gaokao shouldn't be solely based on scores, but should incorporate various special talents for admission?"

"Yes, that way it's more holistic, instead of forcing us to struggle with a subject we don't like. I think there are major problems with China's current education system and the Gaokao!" the high school student said.

Chen Guiliang asked, "What about students from rural areas?"

"Huh?" The high school student didn't understand.

Chen Guiliang said, "I attended a village primary school. The entire school had only two teachers, and they enrolled new students once every three years. One teacher had to teach all the subjects. I went to a township middle school, where the English teacher pronounced 'duck' as 'dui-k,' and the music teacher only taught a few children's songs. According to your proposal, how am I supposed to... my special talents? Raiding birds' nests? Swimming in the river? Or maybe fighting with thugs? Should the Gaokao give extra points based on who killed more thugs?"

The high school student was stunned.

Chen Guiliang said, "Rural students are also recipients of China's education. What kind of quality education can they receive? You find having too much tutoring annoying; you don't like your private tutor. But there are countless rural students who can't even afford tutoring fees, let alone know what a private tutor is. They've never even heard the term 'cram school'!"

At this point, the recording of the show had gone completely off-topic.

But Miss Shen thought it was pretty good and didn't intervene. "So you think the reform towards quality education should be slowed down?"

Chen Guiliang said, "What this young student just described isn't quality education at all. Or rather, to talk about quality education without considering basic education is just a load of shameless crap. That's not quality education, that's elite education, which means abandoning the vast majority of underprivileged students to cultivate only a small group of elites in the cities! The United States is a capitalist country, they have reasons to do that, but we are a socialist country!"

(End of this chapter)
